title: Sample adequacy and saturation
core_position: Core texts commonly use purposive/theoretical sampling and some discuss saturation, especially in grounded theory and applied design; contemporary core sources also stress emergent design and judgement.
external_positions: Information power treats adequacy as a function of aim, specificity, theory, dialogue and analysis. Braun and Clarke reject saturation for reflexive TA. Grounded-theory traditions retain method-specific forms of theoretical saturation or sufficiency.
why_they_differ: They address different analytic logics: finite category development, open-ended interpretation, idiographic depth and sequential collections do not have the same stopping condition.
practical_consequence: A platform must not display a universal saturation meter or minimum sample number. It should ask for the methodology-specific adequacy rationale.
can_they_be_combined: Information power can support planning in many interview studies; theoretical sampling/sufficiency can govern grounded theory. Do not import saturation into reflexive TA merely as a publication convention.
risk_of_mixing_them: Premature stopping, false certainty, inflated samples, or incoherent claims of methodological rigour.

title: What a qualitative interview produces
core_position: Core sources range from interviews as access to experience and attitude to active, ethnographic and interactionally produced accounts.
external_positions: Active-interview and discursive scholars treat accounts as co-produced; realist and phenomenological traditions retain qualified experiential reference.
why_they_differ: They make different ontological claims about language, experience and the relation between account and world.
practical_consequence: Interview protocols, transcription, coding and claims must be tagged with an interview epistemology.
can_they_be_combined: A study can analyse both experiential content and interactional production if it explicitly develops dual questions and evidence standards.
risk_of_mixing_them: Naive truth claims or, in the opposite direction, denying any experiential value to participant accounts.

title: Focus group as efficient interview versus interactional method
issue: Focus group as efficient interview versus interactional method
core_position: Market-research texts emphasize efficient exploration and moderator technique; sociological and handbook sources emphasize norms and interaction.
external_positions: Kitzinger and Wilkinson treat interaction, power, agreement and dissent as data.
why_they_differ: Applied decision research may prioritize content, while interactional and critical traditions study collective meaning-making.
practical_consequence: The unit of analysis and recording requirements must be declared before analysis.
can_they_be_combined: Yes, by conducting content and interactional analyses without treating individual turns as independent observations.
risk_of_mixing_them: Serial interviewing, false consensus and misrepresentation of dominant speakers as group opinion.

title: Ethnographic duration and field boundaries
core_position: Core ethnography emphasizes extended engagement, everyday contexts and progressive focusing; digital and multi-sited developments are recognized.
external_positions: Multi-sited and patchwork ethnography allow distributed sites and repeated shorter engagements; digital ethnography treats online/offline relations as embedded.
why_they_differ: Contemporary lives and researcher conditions challenge a bounded-site, uninterrupted-immersion ideal.
practical_consequence: Duration alone cannot authenticate ethnography; relational and contextual depth must be evidenced.
can_they_be_combined: Yes. A patchwork or multi-sited design can retain reflexive field relations, strategic following and deep contextual analysis.
risk_of_mixing_them: Calling thin online observation or a few visits ethnography, or excluding legitimate researchers because they cannot sustain traditional immersion.

title: Case-study generalization
core_position: Core sources include interpretive particularity, cross-case explanation and business theory-building.
external_positions: Stake stresses the particular and naturalistic generalization; Yin analytic generalization; Eisenhardt theory-building; Flyvbjerg falsification and context-dependent expertise.
why_they_differ: They define the case and purpose differently and use different philosophies of inference.
practical_consequence: A case-study record must include a generalization field rather than a generic representativeness field.
can_they_be_combined: Some designs can combine thick case interpretation with analytic propositions or cross-case comparison, but not by silently mixing criteria.
risk_of_mixing_them: Either overgeneralizing a convenient case or dismissing case knowledge as inherently anecdotal.

title: Grounded-theory emergence, procedure and construction
core_position: The core recognizes grounded-theory coding, constant comparison and theory generation, with both objectivist and constructivist influences.
external_positions: Glaserian emergence/minimal forcing, Straussian procedural coding and constructivist co-construction diverge.
why_they_differ: They differ on ontology, researcher role, prior literature, coding architecture and what counts as theory.
practical_consequence: The platform must require a grounded-theory variant and disable incompatible defaults.
can_they_be_combined: Techniques may be borrowed only with explicit justification; a hybrid cannot claim purity in one school.
risk_of_mixing_them: Mechanical coding, false saturation, theory-by-label and contradictory quality criteria.

title: Themes emerge versus themes are generated
issue: Themes emerge versus themes are generated
core_position: Some core texts use emergence language generically; the current SAGE thematic-analysis chapter presents reflexive theme construction.
external_positions: Reflexive TA treats themes as analytic constructions; coding-reliability approaches may treat coding categories as more stable and reproducible.
why_they_differ: Different TA families have different researcher-subjectivity and reliability assumptions.
practical_consequence: The platform should not use one theme-development workflow for all TA projects.
can_they_be_combined: Codebook structure and reflexive interpretation can coexist in some pragmatic projects, but should not be mislabelled as pure reflexive TA.
risk_of_mixing_them: Methodological mash-up, passive claims of objectivity and inappropriate agreement metrics.

title: Intercoder reliability
core_position: Systematic coding texts value code definitions, team consistency and auditability; critical/reflexive handbooks treat subjectivity as constitutive.
external_positions: O'Connor and Joffe support ICR in appropriate structured designs; Braun and Clarke reject it as a quality criterion for reflexive TA.
why_they_differ: One model treats code application as classifiable agreement; the other treats multiple readings as legitimate interpretive production.
practical_consequence: Reliability calculations must be method-gated and accompanied by a rationale.
can_they_be_combined: Use calibration or dialogic comparison without a reliability statistic in reflexive work; use formal ICR only when code reproducibility is an actual design goal.
risk_of_mixing_them: False validity from a high coefficient or avoidable inconsistency in a classification-oriented project.

title: Member checking as validation
core_position: Trustworthiness traditions often recommend participant feedback; critical and constructionist sources complicate authority and changing interpretations.
external_positions: Birt et al. treat member checking as a flexible dialogic technique rather than automatic truth verification.
why_they_differ: Participants and researchers may hold different legitimate interpretive positions and accounts change over time.
practical_consequence: The platform should ask what was returned, to whom, for what purpose and how disagreement was handled.
can_they_be_combined: Yes, as participant reflection, factual correction, ethical consultation or analytic dialogue, not as a universal pass/fail test.
risk_of_mixing_them: Delegating analytic responsibility, coercing endorsement or claiming validity because participants agreed.

title: Triangulation as confirmation versus expansion/divergence
core_position: Core sources use triangulation for corroboration, multiple perspectives and mixed evidence; some critical chapters resist a single truth model.
external_positions: Mixed-method literature treats integration as convergence, complementarity, expansion and productive discordance.
why_they_differ: Confirmation assumes a common object and error model; interpretive traditions may see methods as constructing different objects.
practical_consequence: A triangulation record should classify purpose and retain discordant results.
can_they_be_combined: Yes, where researchers specify which findings should converge and which are expected to illuminate different dimensions.
risk_of_mixing_them: Forcing false consensus or treating disagreement as research failure.

title: Counting and prevalence in qualitative research
issue: Counting and prevalence in qualitative research
core_position: Core sources permit counting and qualitative-quantitative complementarity but distinguish small purposive insight from population measurement.
external_positions: Content/framework approaches may use counts; reflexive TA and narrative/phenomenological traditions reject frequency as a criterion of significance.
why_they_differ: Methods have different units, sampling designs and theories of significance.
practical_consequence: The platform must separate corpus frequency, sample prevalence and population prevalence.
can_they_be_combined: Yes, with defined units and careful wording; counts can orient analysis without determining meaning.
risk_of_mixing_them: Pseudo-quantification, false population claims and neglect of rare but consequential cases.

title: Phenomenological description versus interpretation
core_position: Core texts include descriptive, interpretive, post-intentional and IPA forms.
external_positions: Giorgi emphasizes reduction and descriptive structure; van Manen hermeneutic writing; IPA double hermeneutic and idiography.
why_they_differ: They derive from different philosophical lineages and treat bracketing and interpretation differently.
practical_consequence: A phenomenology template must require the named tradition and variant-specific steps.
can_they_be_combined: Philosophical dialogue is possible, but procedural hybrids must explain what is retained and rejected.
risk_of_mixing_them: Generic thematic analysis relabelled phenomenology and unsupported claims about essences.

title: Analytic versus evocative autoethnography
core_position: Core handbooks represent both theory-building and performative/relational forms.
external_positions: Anderson prioritizes analytic theoretical contribution; Ellis and Bochner defend evocative, aesthetic and relational knowledge.
why_they_differ: They disagree over the purposes of social science, evidence, reader response and the role of theory.
can_they_be_combined: Some works can be both analytic and evocative, but a single checklist should not impose one tradition's hierarchy.
risk_of_mixing_them: Dismissal of legitimate genres or weak memoir claiming research status without any stated contribution.

title: Participation as empowerment versus participation as domination
issue: Participation as empowerment versus participation as domination
core_position: Core sources emphasize co-production, dialogue, impact and transformation.
external_positions: Cornwall and Jewkes define participation through power; Cooke and Kothari expose tokenism, tyranny and depoliticization.
why_they_differ: Normative aspirations do not guarantee actual redistribution of resources and authority.
practical_consequence: Participation must be audited stage by stage, including budget, data, authorship and action.
can_they_be_combined: Yes: critical power analysis should be built into participatory governance.
risk_of_mixing_them: Extractive co-design, community burden and false claims of empowerment.

title: Decolonization as broad epistemic reform versus specific political project
issue: Decolonization as broad epistemic reform versus specific political project
core_position: Core critical handbooks use decolonizing language for challenging colonial knowledge, methods and institutions.
external_positions: Linda Tuhiwai Smith and Kovach foreground Indigenous agendas and relational protocol; Tuck and Yang warn that decolonization is not a metaphor detached from land and sovereignty.
why_they_differ: The term travels across disciplines and can lose its material political referent.
practical_consequence: A platform should not offer a universal "decolonized" badge based on procedural completion.
can_they_be_combined: Broader anti-colonial critique can coexist with explicit recognition that Indigenous decolonization has specific political meanings.
risk_of_mixing_them: Appropriation, metaphorization and institutional self-congratulation without material change.

title: Universal qualitative quality criteria versus method-specific criteria
issue: Universal qualitative quality criteria versus method-specific criteria
core_position: Core sources offer trustworthiness, validity, authenticity, auditability and big-tent criteria while also presenting paradigm controversies.
external_positions: Reporting frameworks and big-tent criteria aid transparency; Morse, Braun/Clarke and specialist traditions warn against mechanical universal criteria.
why_they_differ: Methodologies make different truth, subjectivity, representation and action claims.
practical_consequence: Use a universal minimum transparency layer plus method-specific quality modules.
can_they_be_combined: Yes. General questions about coherence, evidence, ethics and transparency can coexist with variant-specific standards.
risk_of_mixing_them: Checklist ritualism, paradigm policing or absence of any evaluative accountability.

title: AI as clerical tool, analytic collaborator or autonomous analyst
issue: AI as clerical tool, analytic collaborator or autonomous analyst
core_position: Older core sources discuss software as support and retain human interpretation; current core is largely silent on operational generative-AI analysis.
external_positions: Morgan reports useful descriptive assistance and proposes query-based analysis; Wachinger and Jayawardene/Ewing report partial alignment/efficiency; Messner et al. identify empirical-boundary and epistemological failures; Jones focuses on transparency.
why_they_differ: Studies use different models, prompts, datasets, methods, comparison criteria and epistemologies; the technology changes rapidly.
practical_consequence: AI support must be method-specific, auditable, optional and human-supervised; evidence should not be generalized across models or methods.
can_they_be_combined: Use AI for bounded, verifiable assistance while preserving human familiarization, interpretation and final authority. Treat autonomous analysis as unsupported.
risk_of_mixing_them: Hallucinated evidence, decontextualization, false reliability, privacy breaches, deskilling and opaque analytic influence.

title: Business pragmatism versus epistemological coherence
core_position: Business texts prioritize the information need, budget, timing and decision; qualitative texts prioritize theory, knowledge claims and reflexivity.
external_positions: Mixed-method and applied-framework literature support pragmatism but still require strand-specific standards and integration logic.
why_they_differ: Managerial usefulness and methodological warrant are related but not identical.
practical_consequence: A professional platform must capture both decision utility and methodological legitimacy.
can_they_be_combined: Yes, through explicit problem-method fit, transparent assumptions and limits on claims.
risk_of_mixing_them: Fast but invalid insight, or theoretically pure work that does not answer the decision problem.
